title: Higher culture viscosity reduces Anthrobot motility and size

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Higher culture viscosity reduces Anthrobot motility and size

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Culturing Anthrobots in environments more viscous than the protocol baseline decreases both their motility and their size, suggesting that low-viscosity environments favour the growth of functional, larger bots.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We observed that culture environments with higher viscosity levels than the protocol baseline result in decreased motility (Figure S2, Supporting Information) and size (Figure S3, Supporting Information), suggesting that low‐viscosity environments better facilitate the growth of functional bots as well as yield larger bots.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures”. Scope: NHBE-derived Anthrobots in vitro

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.73

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The variables and directional prediction are explicit, and supplemental measurements test the sampled conditions. Limited raw data and microenvironmental confounding weaken the general low-viscosity interpretation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Regress bot size and displacement metrics against defined culture viscosity conditions while holding medium composition and culture age constant.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Viscosity manipulations may alter other matrix properties.

The tested viscosity range and replicate-level values may be incomplete.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.6
data adequacy: 0.5
discriminating power: 0.78
analysis feasibility: 0.87
operationalizability: 0.96

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Size and motile fraction versus culture viscosity are straightforward endpoints. They appear as supporting figures whose underlying values were not deposited. A retest needs those values or a new viscosity series; the public record does not contain a downloadable size and motility table.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare diameter and motile fraction of Anthrobots grown above the protocol viscosity with baseline low-viscosity cultures, holding seeding density fixed. Lower motility and smaller size at higher viscosity would support the reported effect; no change, or a size change without a motility change, would weaken the joint claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The viscosity series is in supporting figures, with the measurements available on request.

The number of bots and the viscosity values are not in an open table.

Raising matrix concentration changes biochemical cues as well as viscosity.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.9
analysis feasibility: 0.22
data adequacy: 0.18
data existence: 0.2
